assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their joint work on endogenous growth in the open economy, innovation and trade, and the political economy of trade protection (the 'protection for sale' framework) changed both theory and empirical practice. It links trade, growth and political economy in a way that is general and influential across fields.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are the clear core pair for the growth-trade and protection-for-sale work. Helpman also has separate firm-heterogeneity contributions that overlap with B030, but a two-person prize for the joint body of work is coherent.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from the late 1980s to the 1990s and have had decades of confirmation, extension and use in policy and empirical work. Timing is not a constraint.
uncertainties: Krugman's 2008 prize covered part of the new trade theory territory, so the committee may see overlap.
Helpman's separate firm-heterogeneity contributions could complicate how the credit is framed or split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: They built the modern formal political economics of electoral rules, constitutions, fiscal policy and state capacity, and brought rigorous empirical testing to it. The influence on public finance, development and comparative politics is broad and deep.
assessment.attribution: Persson, Tabellini and Besley are the usual central names, with Persson and Tabellini linked through their book and constitutional-design papers and Besley through state capacity and accountability. Other contributors (Acemoglu, Alesina, Dixit) are outside this ballot entry, so the credited trio is defensible but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: The key work spans the 1990s to the 2010s and is well confirmed, with large follow-on literatures. The field is established.
uncertainties: Disclosure: to my knowledge Persson is affiliated with IIES, my own institution, and I have collaborated in the same field network. I disclose this without adjudicating it.
Overlap with other political-economy or institutions-based prizes may affect how the committee frames the contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore collateral-constraint mechanism explains how small shocks are amplified and persist through credit-market frictions. It is central to modern macro-finance and to understanding financial crises and policy responses.
assessment.attribution: The 1997 credit-cycles paper is a clear joint contribution by Kiyotaki and Moore. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the related financial-accelerator line, which is conceptually distinct, so a two-person prize keeps the credit precise.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of use, and the 2008 crisis gave strong empirical and policy validation, so it is mature.
uncertainties: The financial-accelerator and Bernanke-Gertler lineage overlaps and may be treated as part of the same contribution.
The committee may prefer a broader macro-finance prize that combines this with B042 or other credit-cycle work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underlies the modern theory and practice of monetary policy and inflation targeting. It is a foundational, policy-relevant synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Credit is diffuse. Calvo (pricing), Taylor (rules, staggered contracts), Christiano-Eichenbaum (estimated DSGE), Smets (applied DSGE) and others all contributed. Woodford, Gali and Gertler are the most identifiable consolidators of the canonical framework, but the choice is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of development and central-bank use. Maturity is high, though the framework has been challenged and extended since 2008 and 2021-23.
uncertainties: Selecting at most three from a large field risks omitting Taylor, Calvo or Christiano-Eichenbaum.
Recent debates about inflation dynamics and heterogeneous-agent extensions (B048) could affect how the framework is judged.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of labour demand, polarisation, trade adjustment and regional disruption. They are among the most influential empirical labour and trade results of the last two decades, with direct policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task and trade strands. Dorn and Hanson are core to the China-shock papers. Katz and Acemoglu are associated with related technology-and-inequality work, so omitting Katz is a choice rather than a clear error.
assessment.maturity: The key papers are from the 2000s to 2010s and are well replicated and debated, though the long-run interpretation of the China shock is still being refined.
uncertainties: The size and persistence of the China-shock effects are still debated.
The task framework overlaps with other work on technology and wage inequality that may be credited elsewhere.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Using population-scale administrative data, this work transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility, neighbourhood effects and the long-run impacts of policy. It combines methodological innovation with substantial empirical findings.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the dominant figure. Hendren and Friedman are core collaborators on the mobility, neighbourhood and teacher-value-added work. Katz is credited in the entry but is more tied to the Moving to Opportunity strand, so the choice is partly a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: The work is mostly from the 2010s, so it is younger than the other leading candidates. Replication and long-run validation are still in progress.
uncertainties: Relatively short time since the main results; some findings, such as neighbourhood effects, are still debated.
Chetty's wide-ranging output (see also B045) makes the scope of any prize citation hard to define.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework showed how distortions across firms and sectors can explain large cross-country income and productivity gaps. It reorients growth and development accounting and gives a measurable channel for policy.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow wrote the seminal 2009 paper, and Restuccia and Rogerson developed the closely related theoretical line. Rogerson is not on this entry, which may weaken the attribution.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years of widespread use and extension, with some debate over measurement and interpretation. Maturity is moderate to high.
uncertainties: Measurement criticisms (e.g. markup versus distortion, measurement error) affect interpretation.
Rogerson's absence and the closely related Restuccia-Rogerson work complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of optimal use of exhaustible resources, its linkage to growth and welfare, and later work on natural capital and inclusive wealth are foundational for environmental and resource economics and for sustainability measurement. The work bears on how economics treats natural limits and long-run welfare.
assessment.attribution: The 1974 Dasgupta-Heal resource-depletion paper and the related book are joint. Dasgupta also has separate work on population, institutions and the 2021 biodiversity review. Solow, Stiglitz and Hotelling contributed to the same lineage and are not on this entry.
assessment.maturity: The core theory is about 50 years old and well established. Inclusive-wealth and biodiversity applications are newer and less settled.
uncertainties: Disclosure: my own research is in climate and environmental economics, so I may be closer to or more favourable toward this area; I disclose this without adjudicating it.
The Nobel recognition of Nordhaus and the resource-economics lineage may reduce the perceived marginal contribution.
Credit may be split across a wider set of authors (Solow, Stiglitz) and across theory versus policy contributions.
